content.title: Pavement Management Program
content.summary: The City of Arvada manages a Pavement Management Program that includes various contractors for pavement resurfacing, maintenance, and concrete work. Each year, roads are designated for different treatments based on their condition, with options for preventative maintenance and more intensive repairs. Upcoming work areas and schedules for repaving, concrete replacement, and surface treatments can be accessed through linked resources, and information about completed work in 2026 is available on the Progress webpage.
content.body:
## Current updates

**Use the links below to see upcoming work areas.**The City manages several contractors to complete pavement resurfacing, maintenance, and concrete work throughout Arvada. Additional details about what to expect during construction can be found below the project area map.

- [Repaving schedule](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xzCwJ6l2Pky3bvlA4DITyEySfhNxtUuYdn-Hb5u9OrY/edit?usp=sharing) (mill and overlay)
- [Concrete replacement schedule](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1s3q7A6vDbcpXi2ZQopT37ykGmbYpg4rAE4BQkTapsSA/edit?usp=sharing)
- [Surface treatments schedule](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-uMPA0lyWrgvxe95TgyIchVVjsNygYe7olUXgyOhfXM/edit?usp=sharing) (crack, slurry, and cape seals)

Visit the [Progress webpage](/1537) for details on work completed in 2026.

## Overview

Each year the City designates a variety of roads to apply different treatments to based on the current quality of the road. Some are preventative and some are for repair or replacement. For more information about the program, [visit the Understanding the Pavement Program webpage](/1299).

## 2026 Proposed Work Areas

Proposed areas are dependent on the annual budget and weather. Click the map to enlarge and view specific areas. Navigate through the tabs below the map to learn more about each treatment type.

This information is also available alongside other City projects in a searchable map on the [Public Improvements Project page](/612).

**Visit the [Progress webpage](/1537) for details on work completed to date in 2026!**

1. [Repaving (Rehab)](#tabfb40f677-fe4a-40a1-abc0-b361e1af9b21_0)

## Rehabilitation work

Once a road falls into a level of disrepair, maintenance treatments are no longer effective. More cost intensive work must be completed to repair the road.

**Mill and Overlay**grinds down the existing roadway, sometimes just edges, other times the whole width of the road, to remove old asphalt, place subgrade material (if applicable), conduct patching of damaged asphalt, and place the overlay of asphalt.

- Lane markings will be placed after the asphalt is replaced. The timing of this work may vary.

**Full Reconstruction**removes the entire roadway structure repairing sub-base roadway material, then replacing with all new intermediate and overlay asphalt.

- Full reconstruction is more resource intensive work and typically performed separately from this program.

1. [Surface Treatments (maintenance)](#tabfb40f677-fe4a-40a1-abc0-b361e1af9b21_1)

## Preventative maintenance work

Seals are maintenance efforts to help **prevent****damage** and **maintain road quality** to extend the life of the road and avoid more cost intensive and disruptive work.

**Surface treatments**can include various types of work:

- **Crack Seal**protects from water intrusion and other damaging factors. This is one of the most cost-effective preventative maintenance strategies in reducing asphalt deterioration and prolonging pavement life.
- **Cape Seal**is chip seal combined with a slurry seal that makes the material more durable and smoother.
  - **Cape Seal is a 2-step process.** This involves applying a chip seal with a more gravel-like texture, allowing that to set, and then returning several weeks later to apply a slurry seal for a smooth finish.
- **Slurry Seal** applies a thin restorative surface treatment that extends the useful life of asphalt by keeping air and water out and stopping oxidation. During the first year after treatment on hot summer days, Slurry Seal can become soft. This is normal and to be expected.
- **Hot Chip Seal**uses a combination of a liquid asphalt emulsion and a thin layer of open-graded friction course (rock). This process provides a durable surface and waterproof membrane that will improve the existing asphalt.

1. [Concrete](#tabfb40f677-fe4a-40a1-abc0-b361e1af9b21_2)

**Concrete replacement**takes place in areas where asphalt work is planned in future years. Concrete is replaced when:

- The existing curb ramps do not meet ADA standards.
- The existing curb and gutter damage may affect the integrity of future paving.

Please visit the [sidewalk maintenance page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/501) for more information about property owner responsibilities for maintaining sidewalks.

## What to Expect

- **No parking signs**will be placed 24 to 48 hours before work is scheduled to begin
  - Keep in mind that weather or unforeseen circumstances may cause delays
  - **Vehicles may be towed**to a neighboring block
  - Other obstructions in the street, like roll-off dumpsters, are subject to fines and can cause work to be delayed or canceled
- **Work hours**are typically 7am-7pm, Monday through Friday
  - Night-time and weekend work may be allowed in some locations
- **Driveway access**may be limited at times during the work
  - If you need accommodations, please contact us as soon as possible
  - Emergency access will be maintained at all times
- **Turn off sprinklers for concrete work**to avoid water damage which can result in re-work
  - Please **notify the contractor as soon as possible of any sprinkler damage.**Damage will be repaired. If the homeowner completes repairs separately no refunds will be provided.
- **Landscaping or fencing** in the public right-of-way may need to be removed or trimmed back for concrete work. Installation in the public right of way is not allowed per Arvada municipal code [section 4-7-2](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=LADECOARCO_CH4ENSIDE_ART4-7FEWA). The contractor is not responsible for replacing landscaping or fencing removed during construction. Contractors will replace topsoil.
- **Lane closures or lane shifts** may be necessary to complete work
- Heavy machinery, loud noises, dust, and vibrations may be present

Please use caution when driving in areas of heavy equipment, especially if you live on or near a cul-de-sac.

### Keep in Mind

- Fresh pavement is hot, oily and extremely sticky. Try to avoid new pavement when walking.
- To remove sticky tar or asphalt from car or shoes, use fresh soap and water or a citrus-based cleaner. Do not use petroleum-based cleaners.

## Learn more

Listen to the Inside Arvada podcast episode about the Pavement Program using the player below or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/16782583-inside-arvada-s-pavement-program-with-ben-sawaya)(with transcript).
